liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Playin' in the Band Reprise** (1 review, 1 other source): Fans joined arms in a big dance circle during Playin' in the Band; Playin' opens a sequence through Wharf Rat, Drums and Goin' Down the Road, returning to Playin' [1][10]
- **Loser** (1 other source): Crowd fadeout at the end of Loser was reversed and crossfaded into Lazy Lightning [7]
- **Lazy Lightning** (1 other source): Lazy Lightning segues into Supplication in this source's setlist [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **Lazy Lighting-Supplication**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 3 archived performances [21]
- **PITB reprise**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd1976-08-02.132697.aud.gatto.wise.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 25 songs; 201 min; rated 4.5/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd1976-08-02.152092.aud.petrunis.andrewf.flac2448**: audience recording; 26 songs; 198 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [2]. Said about its sound: Tapes held up well after 45 years; sound is clear, with some intrusive crowd noise [2]
- **gd76-08-02.gatto.aj.245.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 194 min; rated 4.12/5 by 26 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience tape has lots of chatter from people near the stage defending their spot; reviewer says it doesn't sparkle; Recording sounds excellent, but a nearby person keeps clapping into the microphones; Very good sound for an early audience tape, though plenty of clapping is audible [11][17][20]
- **gd1976-08-02.145157.sony.ecm99a.warburton.lee.smith.sirmick.flac1644**: source not stated; 24 songs; 197 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [4]
- **gd1976-08-02.fob.singer.motb-1.81456.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 23 songs; 174 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls hearing on the radio driving home to Massachusetts about incredible music at the Hartford Dead show [9]
- Band's limo passed outside before the show and waved; the reviewer drank beer under an oak tree [10]
- Outdoor concert was scheduled for 6 pm, but something unexpected happened at 3 in the afternoon [12]
- Entry was hot and heavy with serious searches; people passed drugs and booze back along the line to avoid seizure [13]
- Reviewer recalls two encores, which was rare, guessing it nodded to Jerry's birthday [13]
- Reviewer was 17, from central Connecticut, and this was their first Dead show after years of listening to albums [18]
- Reviewer notes that Barlow, Weir's lyricist, attended college in Middletown, Connecticut [18]
- Crowd outside broke down barriers, burned snow fencing, and threw rocks and bottles at firemen; riot police arrived as the show ended [19]
- Reviewer thinks many other 1976 shows are musically better than this one [11]
- Reviewer calls this show as good as the one days later at Roosevelt Stadium in Jersey City [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1976-08-02.132697.aud.gatto.wise.flac16**: taped by Keith J. Gatto; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Cassette Audience Master recorded By Keith Gatto; Shure SM 94 microphones-Sony TC 152sd Cassette Recorder; Analog to Digital:Cassette Masters played back on… [1]
- **gd1976-08-02.152092.aud.petrunis.andrewf.flac2448**: taped by Concert recording by Rich Petrunis.; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 03/2021; source: Source: Mono Sony hand-held recorder (model unknown) > Memorex MRX-2 C90's (normal bias). [2]. Also: Mono patches from another source were added, including all of Promised Land and Mississippi Half Step; Tapes came from John and Rich Petrunis [2]
- **gd76-08-02.gatto.aj.245.sbeok.shnf**: taped by K. Gatto; source: Audience Recording [3]. Also: In this download the encores sit at the end of disc 2, and the reviewer left them there; Reviewer fit the encores on disc three using an ogg vorbis download [15][20]
- **gd1976-08-02.145157.sony.ecm99a.warburton.lee.smith.sirmick.flac1644**: taped by Jimmy Warburton; transferred by Matt Smith & Sirmick & Pat Lee; source: Sony ECM 99A > Sony TC 152 > Cassette Master > reel - Recorded by Jimmy Warburton and provided by Pat Lee [4]. Also: Small patches from the Gatto/Wise source cover tape flips; Pat Lee supplied his copy and Matt Smith did the transfer; Source is a Sony ECM99A recording made by Jimmy Warburton at the show [4]
- **gd1976-08-02.fob.singer.motb-1.81456.sbeok.flac16**: taped by E. Singer; transferred by D. McCabe and SirMick; source: Audience FOB Recording [7]. Also: Tape was paused between most tracks, so crossfades were added to smooth transitions; Several artifacts were cleaned up, including a patch in disc 2 track 3 [7]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Grateful Dead@ Colt Park, CT 1976](https://www.dead.net/fanphotos/grateful-dead-colt-park-ct-1976) [22]
- Poster by Worthpoint: [GRATEFUL DEAD 1976 Ticket COLT PARK Hartford CT | #2094838142](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/grateful-dead-1976-ticket-colt-park-2094838142) [23]
